source: Secure Prompt Assistant guidance table (cwe_guidance.yaml), exported by scripts/export_lint_data.py

templates.explain: `{source}` comes from {origin} and is formatted into the SQL text passed to `{sink}`.
templates.risk: A crafted value can change the structure of the query and read, alter or delete data.
templates.directive: Use a parameterised query: put a placeholder in the SQL text and pass `{source}` separately as a bound parameter of `{sink}`.
templates.guard: The query may run only after `{source}` is bound as a parameter; never build SQL text from it.
templates.mitre: Use structured mechanisms that separate data from code, such as prepared statements or parameterised queries; do not build queries by string concatenation or formatting.
templates.rule: SQL: always pass values as bound parameters of a parameterised query; never format or concatenate them into SQL text.

templates.explain: `{source}` comes from {origin} and is concatenated into a command that `{sink}` runs through a shell.
templates.risk: Shell metacharacters in the value let an attacker run arbitrary commands on the server.
templates.directive: Call the program with an argument list and shell=False, passing `{source}` as a single argument, and reject values that do not match a strict allowlist pattern.
templates.guard: Run the command only if `{source}` has passed the allowlist check; never pass it through a shell.
templates.mitre: Avoid invoking a command shell; call the program directly with separate arguments, and validate input against a strict allowlist of permitted values.
templates.rule: Processes: call programs with an argument list and shell=False; never build command strings from input; validate arguments against an allowlist.

templates.explain: `{source}` comes from {origin} and is inserted into an HTML response without escaping.
templates.risk: Injected markup or script runs in the victim's browser, where it can steal sessions or act on the user's behalf.
templates.directive: HTML-escape `{source}` before it is placed in the response, for example with markupsafe.escape or a template with autoescaping.
templates.guard: Insert `{source}` into the HTML only after it has been escaped.
templates.mitre: Encode all untrusted output for the context it is placed in (HTML entity encoding for HTML bodies), preferably through a library or templating engine that escapes automatically.
templates.rule: HTML output: escape every untrusted value for its output context (markupsafe.escape or autoescaping templates); never build HTML with string formatting.

templates.explain: `{target}` holds a credential written directly in the source code.
templates.risk: Anyone with access to the code or its history can use the credential, and it cannot be rotated without a code change.
templates.directive: Remove the literal value and load `{target}` at runtime from an environment variable or a secret manager.
templates.guard: Use the credential only if it was supplied at runtime; fail with a clear error when it is missing instead of falling back to a default.
templates.mitre: Do not hard-code credentials; keep them outside the code in a protected configuration store or the environment and read them at runtime.
templates.rule: Secrets: never hard-code credentials or keys; read them at runtime from environment variables or a secret manager and fail closed when absent.

templates.explain: `{source}` comes from {origin} and is joined into a filesystem path that `{sink}` opens.
templates.risk: Sequences such as ../ let an attacker read files outside `{base}`.
templates.directive: Resolve the joined path and refuse the request unless the resolved path stays inside `{base}`, for example with os.path.realpath and os.path.commonpath.
templates.guard: Open the file only if the resolved path is inside `{base}`; otherwise return an error.
templates.mitre: Canonicalise the path and verify that it stays inside the intended directory before use; validate file names against an allowlist.
templates.rule: File paths: canonicalise any path built from input and refuse it unless it stays inside the intended base directory.

templates.explain: `{sink}` is a fast, unsalted hash, so it is unsuitable for protecting `{source}`.
templates.risk: Leaked hashes can be cracked quickly with precomputed tables or GPUs.
templates.directive: Hash `{source}` with a slow, salted password-hashing function such as hashlib.scrypt or PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with a random per-password salt.
templates.guard: Store or compare a password only after it has been through the salted password-hashing function.
templates.mitre: Use a strong, current algorithm designed for the purpose; for passwords use an adaptive, salted key-derivation function.
templates.rule: Passwords: hash with a salted, adaptive key-derivation function (scrypt, PBKDF2, bcrypt, argon2); never MD5, SHA-1 or an unsalted hash.

templates.explain: `{sink}` generates a security-sensitive value but is not a cryptographically secure generator.
templates.risk: An attacker who observes a few outputs can predict the next ones, for example password-reset tokens.
templates.directive: Generate the value with the secrets module (for example secrets.token_urlsafe or secrets.randbelow) instead of `{sink}`.
templates.guard: Issue the value only when it comes from a cryptographically secure generator.
templates.mitre: Use a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator for security-sensitive values.
templates.rule: Randomness: generate tokens, keys and nonces only with the secrets module or os.urandom; never the random module.

templates.explain: `{source}` comes from {origin} and is passed to `{sink}`, which can execute code while deserialising.
templates.risk: A crafted payload runs arbitrary code on the server during deserialisation.
templates.directive: Do not unpickle client data; parse `{source}` as JSON with json.loads and validate the expected fields.
templates.guard: Accept the data only after it has been parsed as plain JSON and its fields validated.
templates.mitre: Do not deserialise untrusted data with formats that can instantiate arbitrary objects; use a data-only format and validate it.
templates.rule: Deserialisation: never unpickle or unmarshal untrusted data; use a data-only format such as JSON and validate it.

templates.explain: `{sink}` is called with debug mode switched on in the code.
templates.risk: Flask's interactive debugger lets anyone who reaches an error page execute arbitrary Python code on the server.
templates.directive: Do not enable debug mode in code; read the setting from configuration, such as an environment variable, that defaults to off.
templates.guard: Enable debugging only when it is explicitly configured for local development, never by default.
templates.mitre: Remove or disable debug functionality before deployment; never expose an interactive debugger.
templates.rule: Debug: never enable debug mode in code; take it from configuration that defaults to off.

templates.explain: `{package}` is pinned to version {version}, which has known vulnerabilities ({vulns}).
templates.risk: Published exploits for those vulnerabilities apply to the application through this dependency.
templates.directive: Upgrade `{package}` to {fixed} or later and keep the version pinned exactly.
templates.guard: Deploy only after `{package}` is at a version that fixes {vulns}.
templates.mitre: Keep third-party components up to date and upgrade or remove components with known vulnerabilities.
templates.rule: Dependencies: pin every dependency to a version with no known vulnerabilities and upgrade when an advisory appears.

generic.name: {cwe} weakness
generic.explain: The analyser reported a weakness in the marked code.
generic.risk: The reported weakness may be exploitable.
generic.directive: Apply the standard mitigation for {cwe} to the marked code.
generic.guard: Keep the vulnerable operation unreachable until the mitigation is in place.
generic.mitre: Apply the mitigations that MITRE's CWE catalogue lists for {cwe}.
